title: Types, Expressions, and Safe Input
summary: Use integer and floating types, declarations, conversions, format specifiers, arithmetic, and checked text input.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Types, Expressions, and Safe Input
Compile and test behavior with warnings enabled
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: C objects have declared types that determine representation and operations. Integer division truncates toward zero, so cast before division when a fraction is required. `sizeof` reports storage in bytes as `size_t`. `printf` and `scanf` format specifiers must match argument types; a mismatch can cause undefined behavior. For robust interactive input, read a line with `fgets`, then parse with `strtol` while checking the end pointer and range. Initialize objects before reading them and never assume failed input leaves a useful value.
keyPoints: C objects have declared types that determine representation and operations.
